internal.title: Incident Summary: Cart Service High Error Rate
internal.body:
On 2026-11-08 at 10:15 UTC, the cart service experienced a high error rate of approximately 50%, triggering the ServiceErrorRateHigh alert. Initial diagnosis rounds considered error injection, latency, and resource exhaustion as potential causes. Resource exhaustion was refuted due to moderate CPU and minimal memory usage. Latency was considered but not deemed the primary cause. Error injection was supported by the high error rate metric but the proposed remediation action (service restart) was blocked due to missing dry-run validation, causing delays in resolution.

The incident was escalated for further investigation. Recovery actions were not fully executed during the incident window, so a definitive root cause attribution remains pending further validation.

Lessons learned include the importance of ensuring all remediation actions have validated dry-run procedures to avoid blocking critical recovery steps, and the need for clearer diagnostic signals to distinguish between error injection and other fault types in high error rate scenarios.
